newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW - UK December PMI survey.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - UK December PMI survey.

text.p: Following is a selection of reactions to the UK December PMI survey published at 0930 GMT.
The index fell to 52.5 percent from 54.2 percent in November but still indicated expansion in the manufacturing sector for the seventh consecutive month.

"The 14 percent rise in sterling is weighing very heavily on manufacturers. Sterling's appreciation is certainly responsible for part of the (PMI's weakness) along with the interest rate increase we saw last year. We have already seen that in the CBI survey."

"As far as the Chancellor is concerned, if he doesn't want to raise rates he can use the prices index to justify his position. But the bottom line is that rates will have to go up before the election, so there is a case for biting the bullet and raising rates by 25 basis points early, in January, and maybe avoiding a 50 basis point rise later. Part of the weakness has come from destocking and if that is the case, the inventory overhang is disappearing which bodes well for output later this year."

"The fact is we do get a bit of a dip here which fits with what the CBI reported earlier in December. It will be interesting to see how much of this is due to worries about export demand due to the rise in sterling. It was interesting that total orders are still rising quite strongly. That makes me fairly happy that while we may be seeing perhaps a moderation in the pace of pick up of manufacturing activity, the manufacturing sector is continuing to expand and will continue to contribute to growth this year."
